disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, unit boundaries, bag limits, and registration deadlines can change. Always verify current regulations with the Michigan DNR before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.general: Everyone needs a base license ($11 resident 17-64; $6 youth 10-16; $5 resident senior 65+; $151 nonresident) valid through March 31, 2027. A fur harvester license ($15 resident or nonresident; valid through April 30, 2027) is required to hunt/trap furbearers. Residents hunting coyotes with only a base license still need a fur harvester license Nov. 10-14; residents trapping coyotes always need a fur harvester license. Kill tags (bobcat, fisher, marten, otter) are free, available May 1, 2026 (bobcat tags only through Oct. 31), and must be in the harvester's possession BEFORE harvesting. Nonresidents CANNOT harvest badger, bobcat, fisher, marten, or otter in Michigan. Must be at least 8 years old to obtain kill tags. Persons born on or after Jan. 1, 1960 need hunter education.
license_summary.night_hunting: Coyotes, foxes, opossums, raccoons, skunks, and weasels can be hunted at night; nighttime hunting seasons are the same as regular daylight hunting seasons. Legal furbearer hunting hours are 1/2 hour before sunrise to 1/2 hour after sunset.

verification.confirmation_notes: Data taken from the official 2026 Fur Harvester Regulations Summary (Michigan DNR, michigan.gov), which covers the 2026-27 harvest year (license year runs through April 2027; hunting-hours table explicitly covers January-March 2027, so winter season dates in Jan-Mar are 2027). Season dates, bag limits, kill-tag rules, mandatory registration deadlines, management seasons, and unit/county boundary descriptions were all read from this official source. Unit A = Upper Peninsula except Drummond Island; Units B-H as listed; bobcat, fisher, marten, and otter require free resident kill tags (bobcat tags available May 1-Oct 31) and mandatory registration.
known_gaps: Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in the Michigan summary.
Nonresident kill-tag bag limits are shown as 'N/A' in the bag-limit table (nonresidents cannot harvest badger, bobcat, fisher, marten, or otter).
Opossum/skunk/weasel year-round seasons are stated as harvestable 'year-round... with a valid Michigan fur harvester license' — modeled as continuous.
Bobcat trapping Unit A/B has a split season (Nov 1-14, 2026 and Dec 1, 2026-Jan 18, 2027); both legs are modeled as separate season objects.

Michigan hunting hours (1/2 hour before sunrise to 1/2 hour after sunset) vary by date and zone and are not modeled as single times; the Jan-Mar 2027 table was used to confirm season-year interpretation.
Four western Upper Peninsula counties (Gogebic, Iron, Dickinson, Menominee) are on Central Time; the dataset uses America/Detroit statewide — note the one-hour adjustment for those counties.
Tribal harvest regulations (ceded-territory/tribal member rules) are separate and not modeled.
Trap hardware rules, setbacks, and check times are not modeled.
Damage-control take on private property (no license/permit needed for beaver, coyote, muskrat, opossum, raccoon, skunk, weasel doing damage) is noted but not modeled as a season.
